segments.line: Here's how it starts. You and your little sister Ellie are walking home with a bag of takeaway.
And then you're standing in a narrow street that smells like smoke, donkeys and fish sauce.
Everyone is wearing sheets. Okay, tunics.
with a cart shouts at you in Latin. A coin in the dirt has an emperor's face on it. Nero.
the summer of the year sixty- four, and this is Rome. The biggest city in the world, with around a million people.
So here are the rules. There's no way back.
You have the clothes you're wearing, a phone with no signal, and one cold burger in a paper bag. That's it.
No fridge. No fryer. No electricity. Not one machine.
But you have something nobody else in Rome has. You know exactly how a fast food restaurant works.
The same food, every time, ready in one minute.
And one more thing. Rome, in the summer of sixty- four.
It sounds familiar. Something from history class. You just can't remember what.
